newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia calls for Israeli troop withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia calls for Israeli troop withdrawal.

text.p: Indonesia on Saturday called on Israel to withdraw its troops from Palestinian-ruled areas and urged the U.N. Security Council to meet to take steps to end the violence.

The Indonesian Foreign Ministry said in a statement that Jakarta could not condone Israeli violence against Palestinians in the occupied areas, including Jerusalem, Ramaliah, Nablus and Gaza. "The situation is very grave," the statement said.

"Israel's violent actions have challenged the agreements which are already reached between Israel and the PLO (Palestinine Liberation Organisation), international humanitarian law and clearly will threaten the continuation of the peace process," the statement said.
"The Israeli government must soon stop these actions which are breaking these laws and withdraw its forces from areas which based have already been given over to the Palestinians," it said.
"Indonesia as a non-permanent member of the U.N. Security Council urges the U.N. Security Council to soon meet and take the steps which are needed to stop Israel's violence," it said.

Indonesia is the world's largest Moslem state, with around 85 percent of its more than 195 million people said to be followers of Islam. Jakarta has been a long time supporter of the Palestinian cause.
